content.comment_body: I'm working on a ladder logic program and facing issues using Function Keys F1 to F4 across various menus. For instance, using F1 in one menu also affects another menu where F1 has a separate function. When F1 is pressed, both rungs are triggered unintentionally. My inquiry to [company_name] support has been slow, so I would appreciate any ideas or advice.

You need to link each F-key to its specific message text so that only one message text is active at any time. This means designing your menu so you can select which message text is active, preventing multiple texts from responding simultaneously.
Here is a basic example to illustrate the approach.
Hello, I’ve attached a menu example with the corresponding variable settings. The password to access the menu is 11111. Feel free to reach out if you need further clarification.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is experiencing problems assigning unique actions to function keys F1-F4 for different menus in a ladder logic program. Function keys are currently causing multiple unintended actions due to overlapping activation. Other users recommend restricting function key functionality so that only one menu or message text is active at a time, helping to prevent conflicts.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects context-sensitive behavior from function keys, ensuring each key triggers only the appropriate action for the currently active menu without inadvertently affecting other program areas.
